# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Commit on `main` in the repository's main checkout: no git worktrees, and one agent per
  repository at a time.
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.cad` kit. These rules come first; the
upstream rules below still apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition CAD's Home ribbon, the drawing canvas with the engine's tools, the layers palette, the command line, and the drafting modes; a host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it
  in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's theme tokens and kit-editor components;
  ribbon labels and command titles are the upstream editor's English text, translated by
  `PHRASES` in `web/src/strings.ts` (`en-US` and `zh-CN` strings). Files go only through the
  host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public `KitionAI/kition-sdk`
  crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP (`github.com/kitharness/kitharness`);
  change them there, never here. `kition-cad-kit` must keep passing
  `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`, and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- Tools run in the engine (`KitTools`): pointer, key, and text events in, requests, overlays, and a
  cursor out. A drawing tool is the command of the same name; clicks answer its prompts. Never
  draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- The whole repository is Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)), including the upstream-derived
  crates; third-party notices are listed in `NOTICE`. Upstream is credited only in `NOTICE`;
  never write upstream names anywhere else.

# Kition CAD — instructions for agents

Kition CAD is a clean-room, open-source, pure-Rust computer-aided design and drafting engine targeting Autodesk AutoCAD parity — and superiority (speed, openness, agent control).

See `docs/kits.md` in the Kition repository and kition-sdk's `docs/platform/` for the conventions shared across kits.

## Start every session here
1. Read `plan/STATUS.md` (current milestone, next task), then the task in `plan/execution-plan.md` and the relevant `plan/architecture.md` section. Behaviour reference: `plan/autocad/*` (`01-observed-ui.md` holds measured observations of the running reference app; `04-menu-tree.txt` the menu tree by name).
2. Library decisions: `plan/adr/0001-geometry-libraries.md` (what we may depend on, what is rejected for license reasons).
3. Follow the autonomous operation protocol (`plan/execution-plan.md` §6). Don't stop to ask unless it lists the decision as a maintainer's.

`plan/` is gitignored (local only).

## Never crash
People trust Kition CAD with their drawings; a crash loses their work. **This outranks feature work.**
- **No panics in non-test code:** no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`; no `unsafe` (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`).
- **Errors are `Result<T, E>`** through the crate's error type and `?`. An unfinished feature returns an error or reports "not available yet"; it never panics.
- **Input-derived numbers are hostile** (DXF/DWG files, command-line text, MCP/control params): `get()` not `[i]`, checked arithmetic, no NaN casts, cap input-sized allocations and loop counts.
- **Bound recursion** (nested/cyclic block references: `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`).
- **Last-resort guard:** `Session::execute` and every step of an interactive command (its factory, `begin`, input, `prompt` and `preview`; `crates/engine/engine/src/guard.rs`) run under `catch_unwind`; an escaped panic restores the drawing and reports an error.
- **Prove it:** every crash fix lands with a regression test (see `hostile_params_never_panic`, `hostile_dxf_does_not_panic`).
- Every production crate root carries `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`.

## Non-negotiables
- **Clean-room.** AutoCAD is installed on the dev machine and may be *observed* black-box: run it, use its UI with synthetic drawings, take screenshots (by window id) stored only under `plan/autocad/screenshots/` (never committed). **Never** read, disassemble or copy anything inside the AutoCAD bundle (names/listings only); never copy Autodesk fonts (SHX), hatch patterns (`.pat`), linetypes (`.lin`), templates, CUI/PGP files, icons, artwork or help text; never commit files produced by AutoCAD. File formats come from public specifications (Autodesk's published DXF Reference, the Open Design Alliance's public DWG specification) and our own synthetic tests. Never copy or link GPL/LGPL/AGPL code (LibreDWG, LibreCAD, QCAD, FreeCAD's planegcs, SolveSpace, OpenCASCADE) — don't even read their sources.
- **Assets — absolutely essential.** Kition CAD contains **no Autodesk, Adobe or Avid iconography, images, fonts, patterns or artwork — ever.** Every hatch pattern and linetype is our own definition (`crates/engine/doc/src/library.rs`), the drafting font is our own (`crates/support/fonts/src/stroke.rs`). Any file asset must be original, public domain/CC0, OSI-licensed, or redistributable Creative Commons (or licensed open source by a contributor who made it), and **must have a row in `docs/attribution.md`** with author, source and license (`cargo xtask assets` enforces it). Screenshots of Autodesk software are never committed. Breaking this rule is the most serious mistake you can make in this repo.
- **Shared test corpora** live in separate repos (`KitionAI/kition-cad-corpus`); never commit large binary fixtures here.
- **Everything is a command.** User-visible behaviour = a command in `crates/engine/engine/src/cmd/*` (`CommandSpec`: id = AutoCAD's command name in lower case, label, menu path, shortcut, aliases, params doc, `enabled`, JSON `run`, optional `interactive` prompt machine) + tests. The editor (`web/`) and the headless kit executable both reach the same commands through `KitTools`.
- **Programmatic calls never open dialogs.** `engine.execute` runs the JSON form with defaults; only menu/toolbar invocation starts the interactive prompt sequence.
- **Layering** is enforced by `cargo xtask layers`: L0 `geom`, `dxf` → L1 `color`, `doc` → L2 `fonts`, `render`, `constraints` → L3 `io` → L4 `engine` → L5 `kition-cad-kit` → apps.
- **The UI is thin**: panels read engine state and act through `app.run(id, params)` / `app.start(id)` / `app.cmdline(text)`. Colours come from `theme::Tokens`.
- **Rust only** (no handwritten JS/TS). **Never break wasm** (`cargo xtask wasm`).
- **Checks and CI.** On this machine run only the fast checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p <touched crates> --all-targets`, the wasm check (`cargo xtask wasm`) and `pnpm typecheck` in `web/`. Commit after every feature arc that builds. The full checks run in the kit's CI run on GitHub (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which calls Kition's reusable kit CI): clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm) and every `test:*` script of `web/`. A task is done when the CI run of HEAD passes and HEAD is on `origin/main` (Kition's `scripts/kit-ci.sh` `push`, `wait`, `land`); never push untested commits to `main`. Add no other workflows, and do not start the Package workflow (`.github/workflows/package.yml`): releasing is the owner's step.

## Running and looking at the app
- There is no desktop app, CLI or control channel in this repository (Kition does not use
  them). Drive the engine through `engine::Session` directly in tests, or
  through the headless kit executable: `cargo run --release -p kition-cad`.
- For the in-page editor, run `web/` (`pnpm dev`) and use `web/dev.html` as the host.
- Shell gotcha: `mv`/`cp` may be aliased interactive — use `/bin/mv -f` / `/bin/cp -f`.
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent; edit only the crates you own; delete your target dir when done (disk).

## Roadmap
`docs/gaps.md` lists every known shortfall and `docs/roadmap.md` the order of work, both from the
feature catalogue (`features.yaml`); `docs/parity/target-app-parity.md` gives each feature's status
against AutoCAD. Deep checklists: `docs/parity/geometry-parity.md`, `docs/parity/ui-parity.md`,
`docs/parity/file-format-parity.md`, `docs/parity/hardware-parity.md`,
`docs/parity/localization-parity.md`. When work lands, update the feature in `features.yaml`, then
those three lists, and the affected checklist rows, status lines and revision history. `cargo xtask parity`
regenerates the menu-breadth checklist in `docs/parity/parity-checklist.md`.
